plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates the AlexNet convolutional neural network architecture using a 3D volume diagram viewed in perspective. A left-to-right flow begins with a sheared input photograph representing the 224×224×3 input image, followed by a sequence of three-dimensional feature map volumes rendered as parallelogram-faced blocks in light teal (#d3edeb) for the main face and darker teal (#a0d9d3) for the depth layers, while orange (#d18362) and dark orange (#773c23) parallelogram blocks represent convolutional filter kernels applied at each stage. The feature map volumes progressively shrink in spatial resolution while increasing in depth, with labeled dimensions 55×55×96, 27×27×256, and 13×13×384 corresponding to the first three convolutional stages of AlexNet. Ellipsis (…) markers appear within the teal volume stacks to indicate that only a representative subset of the channels is depicted. A “Conv 5×5” annotation above one inter-stage region identifies the kernel size of one convolution, and black arrows with arrowheads indicate the forward data flow between stages. This figure introduces the AlexNet architecture, showing how successive convolution and pooling operations reduce spatial resolution while extracting increasingly abstract feature representations.

elements: large input image plane at the far left, drawn as a thin vertical 224×224×3 slab with a black border and warm candle-like image texture
dimension callout arrow above the input image labeled 224×224×3
bottom label under the input image reading Conv 11×11 Stride 4
first orange 3D feature-map block labeled 55×55×96
bottom label between input and first block reading MaxPool
bottom label near first block reading Conv 5×5
second orange 3D feature-map block labeled 27×27×256
bottom label after the second block reading MaxPool
third low orange 3D feature-map block labeled 13×13×384
bottom label under the third block reading Conv 3×3
fourth low orange 3D feature-map block labeled 13×13×384
fifth low orange 3D feature-map block labeled 13×13×256
bottom label near the fifth block reading MaxPool + FC
black forward-flow arrows along the baseline between every major layer block
slanted black dimension arrows above each convolutional feature block
first tall teal fully connected column with a broken middle section and vertical ellipsis, labeled 4096
second tall teal fully connected column with a broken middle section and vertical ellipsis, labeled 4096
bottom labels under the two tall teal columns reading FC
first shorter teal output column with a broken middle section and vertical ellipsis, labeled 1000
second shorter teal output column with a broken middle section and vertical ellipsis, labeled 1000
bottom label under the first 1000 column reading FC
bottom label under the final 1000 column reading Softmax
small zigzag break marks on the teal fully connected and output columns
thin black outlines around every image slab, orange block, teal column, arrow, and callout

interactions.label: Convolutional stage
interactions.teaches: Selecting stages 1, 2, and 3 makes the tradeoff explicit: spatial dimensions shrink from 55 to 27 to 13 while channel depth grows from 96 to 256 to 384

demo_steps.title: Stage 1: first convolutional response
demo_steps.narration: The input image is converted into a 55×55×96 feature volume. The large spatial image has already been reduced, but the representation now has many channels.

demo_steps.title: Stage 2: pooled and deeper features
demo_steps.narration: The selected block becomes 27×27×256. Spatial resolution is smaller, while channel depth grows to hold more learned feature detectors.

demo_steps.title: Stage 3: compact high-channel map
demo_steps.narration: The 13×13×384 block is spatially compact but visibly deeper. This emphasizes AlexNet's early pattern: reduce height and width while increasing representational depth.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a left-to-right oblique network layout matching the source. Approximate world coordinates: input slab centered near x=-5.0, y=1.2; first orange block x=-2.4; second x=-1.25; third x=0.15; fourth x=1.25; fifth x=2.35; tall FC bars x=3.45 and x=4.15; output/softmax bars x=5.05 and x=5.75. Front faces should be vertical, with depth receding up-left and the right side face visible. Scale tensor front-face height and width by spatial size but compress for readability: input front face about 2.3×2.3 units, 55×55 blocks about 0.72×0.72, 27×27 blocks about 0.50×0.50, 13×13 blocks about 0.34×0.34. Depth thickness encodes channels: 224×224×3 slab depth 0.04, 55×55×96 depth 0.38, 27×27×256 depth 0.62, 13×13×384 depth 0.82, 13×13×256 depth 0.62. The third and fourth 13×13×384 blocks must be equal size; the fifth 13×13×256 block should have the same front size but shallower depth. FC columns are thin vertical teal stacks: 4096 columns height about 2.9 units, width 0.13, depth 0.12; 1000 columns height about 1.55 units, width 0.13, depth 0.12. Dominant colors: orange front faces #d18362, darker orange side faces #773c23, pale orange top faces #e6a37f; teal front faces #d3edeb, teal side faces #a0d9d3; black outlines/arrows/text #000000; input image approximated with black-to-gold candle texture using #050505, #5b2405, #f5a623, and #ffd35a. Stage slider overlay mapping: stage 1 highlights 55×55×96 and shows Conv 11×11 stride 4; stage 2 highlights 27×27×256 and shows Conv 5×5; stage 3 highlights the first 13×13×384 block and shows Conv 3×3. If the lesson must emphasize the requested Conv 5×5 callout, keep that callout visible above the stage-2 overlay.
interactionPlan.notes: Use an orthographic camera with an oblique projection feel rather than true perspective convergence. Build each volume from front, side, and top meshes with black edge outlines. Animate data flow by moving a glowing yellow outline or pulse along the baseline arrows and briefly brightening each tensor in sequence: input, 55×55×96, 27×27×256, 13×13×384, then fade into later blocks. The layer slider should override the highlight target and display a floating overlay panel near the selected block with kernel size and output dimensions. Drag interaction should rotate only the currently selected tensor block around its center while leaving a faint ghost outline in the original diagram position so the overall architecture remains recognizable.

Stage 1: 55×55×96
The input image is converted into a 55×55×96 feature volume.
Drag the highlighted orange tensor to reveal channel depth.
⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: The input image slab is much more front-facing and square-like than the tall oblique image plane in the source, and the candle image is only a simplified approximation.
The orange feature-map blocks have noticeably different proportions and spacing, with some later blocks appearing too small/flat compared with the source.
The fully connected/output columns are rendered as very thin mostly wire-like segmented bars rather than the wider filled cyan vertical bars in the source.
Several labels are horizontal instead of diagonally aligned with the source callouts, causing merged or cluttered text such as the bottom layer names and paired 4096/1000 labels.
The generated figure adds a yellow stage overlay, data-flow pulse, and interaction UI that are not present in the original static textbook diagram.
evaluation.notes: The AlexNet pipeline is recognizable and mostly complete, but the viewpoint/proportions and label layout are not very faithful to the original figure.
action_items: Use a stronger oblique/isometric viewpoint and rescale the input image, orange tensors, and FC columns to better match the source proportions.
Reposition and rotate dimension and layer labels to follow the diagonal callout style of the source and prevent merged text.
Make the cyan FC/output columns wider and more filled, closer to the original vertical bars.
Remove or visually de-emphasize the yellow overlay and animated pulse when the goal is strict resemblance to the static source figure.

feedback.rationale: The AlexNet concept is correct, but the critic identifies implementation-level fidelity issues—viewpoint, proportions, label rotation, FC bar styling, and extra overlays—that the generator can fix without changing the plan.

discrepancies: The orange convolution feature volumes are noticeably undersized and too cube-like/flat compared with the taller, more substantial cuboids in the source, especially the 55×55×96 and 27×27×256 blocks.
The input image slab is shown more front-on and simplified, with a stylized candle approximation rather than the source's darker oblique image panel with a clear side edge.

Extra interactive teaching elements are visible in the figure area, including the yellow data-flow pulse, halo, highlighted tensor outline, and yellow explanatory overlay, none of which appear in the original printed figure.
The overall vertical emphasis of the source is reduced: the generated architecture is compressed into a lower, flatter horizontal band.
Some dimension labels are placed closer to the blocks and appear more cluttered than the clean separated callouts in the source.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure is clearly recognizable as the AlexNet layer diagram and includes the major labels and layer topology, but the tensor proportions are compressed and several interactive overlays add non-source visual clutter.
action_items: Increase the height and visual mass of the early orange feature volumes, especially 55×55×96 and 27×27×256, to better match the source proportions.
Make the input image panel more oblique with a clearer dark side edge and reduce the front-on square appearance.
Hide the yellow data-flow pulse, halo, highlight, and explanatory overlay by default when matching the static source figure.
Raise and space the dimension callout labels slightly more like the original to reduce clutter around the blocks.

The feature map volumes progressively shrink in spatial resolution while increasing in depth, with labeled dimensions 55×55×96, 27×27×256, and 13×13×384 corresponding to the first three convolutional stages of AlexNet. Ellipsis (…) markers appear within the teal volume stacks to indicate that only a representative subset of the channels is depicted. A “Conv 5×5” annotation above one inter-stage region identifies the kernel size of one convolution, and black arrows with arrowheads indicate the forward data flow between stages. This figure introduces the AlexNet architecture, showing how successive convolution and pooling operations reduce spatial resolution while extracting increasingly abstract feature representations.

interactions.label: Animate data flow
interactions.teaches: The learner sees AlexNet transform one image into progressively smaller spatial maps with more channels, rather than treating the layer list as unrelated boxes

interactions.label: Convolutional stage
interactions.teaches: Selecting stages 1, 2, and 3 makes the tradeoff explicit: spatial dimensions shrink from 55 to 27 to 13 while channel depth grows from 96 to 256 to 384
Rotating the selected tensor reveals that the apparent thickness is channel depth, so later blocks are not just flatter rectangles but deeper feature volumes

demo_steps.title: Stage 1: first convolutional response
demo_steps.narration: The input image is converted into a 55×55×96 feature volume. The large spatial image has already been reduced, but the representation now has many channels.

demo_steps.title: Stage 2: pooled and deeper features
demo_steps.narration: The selected block becomes 27×27×256. Spatial resolution is smaller, while channel depth grows to hold more learned feature detectors.

demo_steps.title: Stage 3: compact high-channel map
demo_steps.narration: The 13×13×384 block is spatially compact but visibly deeper. This emphasizes AlexNet's early pattern: reduce height and width while increasing representational depth.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a left-to-right oblique network layout matching the source. Approximate world coordinates: input slab centered near x=-5.0, y=1.2; first orange block x=-2.4; second x=-1.25; third x=0.15; fourth x=1.25; fifth x=2.35; tall FC bars x=3.45 and x=4.15; output/softmax bars x=5.05 and x=5.75. Front faces should be vertical, with depth receding up-left and the right side face visible. Scale tensor front-face height and width by spatial size but compress for readability: input front face about 2.3×2.3 units, 55×55 blocks about 0.72×0.72, 27×27 blocks about 0.50×0.50, 13×13 blocks about 0.34×0.34. Depth thickness encodes channels: 224×224×3 slab depth 0.04, 55×55×96 depth 0.38, 27×27×256 depth 0.62, 13×13×384 depth 0.82, 13×13×256 depth 0.62. The third and fourth 13×13×384 blocks must be equal size; the fifth 13×13×256 block should have the same front size but shallower depth. FC columns are thin vertical teal stacks: 4096 columns height about 2.9 units, width 0.13, depth 0.12; 1000 columns height about 1.55 units, width 0.13, depth 0.12. Dominant colors: orange front faces #d18362, darker orange side faces #773c23, pale orange top faces #e6a37f; teal front faces #d3edeb, teal side faces #a0d9d3; black outlines/arrows/text #000000; input image approximated with black-to-gold candle texture using #050505, #5b2405, #f5a623, and #ffd35a. Stage slider overlay mapping: stage 1 highlights 55×55×96 and shows Conv 11×11 stride 4; stage 2 highlights 27×27×256 and shows Conv 5×5; stage 3 highlights the first 13×13×384 block and shows Conv 3×3. If the lesson must emphasize the requested Conv 5×5 callout, keep that callout visible above the stage-2 overlay.
interactionPlan.notes: Use an orthographic camera with an oblique projection feel rather than true perspective convergence. Build each volume from front, side, and top meshes with black edge outlines. Animate data flow by moving a glowing yellow outline or pulse along the baseline arrows and briefly brightening each tensor in sequence: input, 55×55×96, 27×27×256, 13×13×384, then fade into later blocks. The layer slider should override the highlight target and display a floating overlay panel near the selected block with kernel size and output dimensions. Drag interaction should rotate only the currently selected tensor block around its center while leaving a faint ghost outline in the original diagram position so the overall architecture remains recognizable.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Animate data flow: sequentially highlight each 3D tensor block from input 224×224×3 through 55×55×96 and 27×27×256 to 13×13×384, displaying the spatial dimensions shrinking and channel depth growing at each conv/pool step

discrepancies: The input candle image is a simplified geometric reconstruction and appears nearly front-on, while the source shows a more photo-like tilted image slab with clearer side depth.
Several orange convolutional volumes are proportionally too squat or compressed compared with the source, especially the first two feature-map blocks.
The yellow selected-stage overlay, yellow highlight, and animated data-flow pulse are extra in-scene elements that do not appear in the source and partially clutter the architecture diagram.
Some dimension callout arrows and labels float near the blocks rather than matching the source's precise arrow-to-edge placement.
The fully connected teal columns are broadly correct but are thinner and more uniformly stylized than the source columns.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure is clearly recognizable as the AlexNet layer diagram with correct major labels and useful interactions, but extra pedagogical overlays and some proportion/view differences reduce visual fidelity.
action_items: Adjust the convolutional block sizes and depths to more closely match the relative proportions in the source figure.
Make the input image slab more oblique and photo-like, with a clearer black side face and less cartoon-styled candle content.
Move or hide the yellow stage overlay and data-flow pulse by default so the static figure more closely matches the textbook source.
Refine the top dimension arrows so each points precisely to the corresponding tensor edge as in the original.

feedback.rationale: The figure has strong concept accuracy and usability with only visual fidelity/proportion issues and optional extra overlays, so it is good enough to stop rather than re-plan or refine.
